---
title: "What the metrics can and cannot tell us"
subtitle: "Paper 6 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-10"
abstract: |
  Every paper in this series except paper 4 has reported a return on
  investment, and the sequence of those figures has been used to judge whether
  each model improved on the one before. This paper shows it cannot support
  that use, drops one of Owen's two scoring rules, refines the other, and
  closes with a labelled first look at a quantity that matches how the model
  would be used rather than how it has been scored.
  Section 1 gives two demonstrations. Of the four consecutive-model
  differences in single-bet win return, recomputed here on one bet rule so the
  four can be read as a sequence, only
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_contrasts, store = S); c("none", "one", "two", "three", "all four")[sum(d$excludes_zero) + 1] })`
  excludes zero, and it is the earliest. Papers 2b and 3 tie on three ranking
  measures with intervals a few per cent of the quantity measured, while the
  interval on their return difference is
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_resolution, store = S); r <- d[d$measure == "single-bet win ROI", ]; sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * r$width_over_value) })`
  of it. Holding the model and the rule fixed and changing only the races, the
  same figure moves
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_race_sets, store = S); sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (d$roi[1] - d$roi[2])) })`
  points between two adjacent sets of races.
  Section 2 drops P1, which reads only the winning rows, and recomputes P2 on
  disjoint bins with finer resolution below 0.10, against two benchmarks: the
  over-round-adjusted settled starting price and the overnight racecard
  forecast price. On
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_p2_cover, store = S); format(d$rows_panel, big.mark = ",") })`
  runner-rows all three models lose to the starting price and all three beat
  the forecast price, six intervals excluding zero. P2 also separates the
  paper-5 encoder from both earlier models, which the return could not, and
  reports papers 2b and 3 as a tie. The bins show the models stating more than
  they win on long prices and less than they win on short ones.
  Section 3 is speculation and nothing in the paper rests on it. Paper 4 found
  the model adds nothing distinguishable against the settled starting price
  and a great deal against the overnight forecast, so this fits how much of
  the model's disagreement with the forecast the market later accepts. The
  pooled coefficient is
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_beta, store = S); sprintf("%.3f", d$estimate[d$term == "slope"]) })`
  with a standard error of
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_beta, store = S); sprintf("%.3f", d$se[d$term == "slope"]) })`.
  A forecast is a published opinion rather than a price anyone bet into, so
  the figure is an upper bound on anything tradeable, and a positive
  coefficient does not establish the idea it came from.
format:
  html: default
  pdf:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Paper 6 reads the paper-6 store. Like papers 4 and 5 and unlike papers 1-3
# this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the project-root
# `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also write, and
# pointing it at `_targets_p6` would send their next render at the wrong
# store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml` untouched.
P6_ROOT <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P6_STORE <- file.path(P6_ROOT, "_targets_p6")

source(file.path(P6_ROOT, "papers", "06_metrics", "_helpers.R"))

# tar_load() centrally so tarchetypes::tar_quarto() picks these up as render
# dependencies — files pulled in via {{< include >}} are not auto-scanned.
tar_load(c(
  # identity and gates
  p6m_race_identity, p6m_basis_check, p6m_recompute_check,
  # section 1a
  p6m_series, p6m_published, p6m_contrasts, p6m_resolution,
  p6m_backtests_main,
  # section 1b
  p6m_val_halves, p6m_race_sets,
  # section 2
  p6m_p2_cover, p6m_p2_all, p6m_p2_diffs, p6m_p2_bins, p6m_p2_order,
  p6m_p2_pairs,
  # section 3
  p6m_beta, p6m_p4_cited, p6m_spread
), store = P6_STORE)
```
